messages:
oncall-bot: PAGED: inference-api (prod) — elevated 5xxs from apac-edge during geo rollout. alert: 25% 5xx, health checks flapping. paging: @Elaine (primary)
Elaine: on it — joining.
Raj: I'm awake, looking at metrics now. apac-edge latency + errors starting ~2m after traffic shift.
Sophia: We kicked a blue->green roll to APAC ~03:12 UTC, target weight 30% green. Dash shows apac receiving ~78% green traffic. EU looks fine.
Mike: Can someone run weight check please? I think the global router didn't apply the partial weights.
Raj: Running checks:
```
# redwoodctl route get-weights --from eu --to apac
eu->apac: desired=30% green, actual=78% green
```
Mike: oof. That explains surge on green. Could be stale edge LB config or DNS not honouring the new weighted config.
Alice: infra-bot shows deploy 2026-03-17T03:11:58 UTC to eu-green completed (sha: a1b2c3). No errors on deploy.
infra-bot: Route-change request accepted: change-id rc-84321.
Sophia: CS reports two APAC customers seeing latency spikes and request failures. CS-Bot: notable customer: Streamflow (APAC) - 120 failed requests in last 5m.
Elaine: We need to reduce blast radius. Options: (1) kill feature flag 'geo-rollout-new-routing' to revert routing, (2) set apac weight back to 0% green, (3) rollback eu-green deploy. Thoughts?
Raj: My vote: flag kill first (fast), then drop apac weight to 0% green. If that doesn't stabilize, rollback deploy.
Mike: Agree. Flag kill is <30s if API healthy. I'll execute.
Mike: Running:
```
curl -s -X POST "https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/geo-rollout-new-routing/kill" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
```
Mike: API responded 200 OK. Flag state: killed -> routing should immediately route to previous variant.
infra-bot: Feature-flag change recorded: geo-rollout-new-routing = OFF (actor: mike)
Elaine: Good. Now adjusting router weights to 0% green for apac as backup.
Raj: Applying weight patch:
```
redwoodctl route set-weights --region apac --green 0
```
Raj: Command accepted. Monitoring.
Sophia: Metrics: apac green traffic dropping from 78% -> 4% over last 40s. 5xx rate trending down.
CS-Bot: Customer Streamflow: errors reduced to single digits, ops ticket updated.
Alice: Note: DNS TTL for edge endpoints is 300s, but we've seen some caches still serving older answers. That likely caused the initial overshoot where traffic continued to the green pool before routers fully respected weights.
Elaine: Forward: set short TTL on rollout records during weighted rollouts. Add to runbook.
Raj: I'm going to keep watches for 15m. If stable, we'll close incident. I'll also kick-off a temporary rollback window for eu-green if error rate regresses.
Sophia: Opening incident ticket: INC-2026-04123 severity=P1, owner=Raj, impact=APAC customers saw increased errors and latency for ~6m.
oncall-bot: Incident channel created: #inc-4123141592. Pager duty notified for P1.
Elaine: Anyone from infra want to check router control plane logs for rc-84321 application ordering? We need root cause: why desired 30% ended up 78%.
Alice: I'll pull logs and search for ordering race vs. broadcast delays. Also capturing controller leader transitions.
Mike: Follow-up: add temporary probe to verify applied weight immediately after route change in future rollouts.
Raj: Confirmed stabilization: last 5m apac 5xx <1%. Latency returned to baseline. Customer notifications sent: Streamflow + 1 other.
Elaine: Handoff in 10m to night on-call. Raj will take post-mitigation and drive postmortem. Please add every action to the incidentticket.
Raj: Will do. Initial RCA hypothesis: router weight broadcast lag + DNS cache TTL interplay causing transient over-shift to new pool. Postmortem will include timeline, commands, and mitigations (flag kill playbook, preflight weight check, TTL guidance).
Sophia: I'll draft customer impact summary for execs.
CS-Bot: Notified customers: template sent to affected customers; tickets linked.
Elaine: Thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep channel open for handoff notes.
oncall-bot: Incident mitigated. Status -> Stable. Please file postmortem within 48h.
Raj: Ack — will own postmortem. Closing active paging.
Elaine: Closing channel after handoff. :white_check_mark:
